Yeah, sorry about that. The formatting for this document is pretty wonky. My goal was to try and replicate handwritten notes, but different browsers and devices tend to display it differently.

Originally, I was actually planning on handwriting these pages and uploading images. However, that never worked. I also realized it would be too hard to replicate, which was one of the stipulations for the contest (I realize that this is also hard to replicate, but I digress). So, this was actually my backup plan, and I suppose that it didn't quite work out either. But, with the time limit of the contest, I think it was as good as I could manage. I've never been good with HTML and CSS.

If I ever get enough free time to jump back in the site, my first goal will be to fix this. I've always wished it had turned out better. Unfortunately, I've been super busy recently and haven't had any time to devote to SCP. Hopefully that will change in the future, but only time will tell.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hey guys. I haven't been active on the site, as I've been real busy with other things. However, I try to keep an eye on it every once in a while, and a message from Voct let me know about this. So, I'll go ahead and give my thoughts.

Short Answer:
3rd description is Chaos Insurgency, 4th is Prometheus Labs, 5th is UIU.

+ Long Answer
- OK, geez sorry I asked

My goal with these Aliases was to spark peoples' imagination with who knows about the object and what they want with it. I also wanted to make formats that felt genuine for each group.

Since in most incarnations, the Chaos Insurgency is all about using anomalies, I wanted a "SCP" type number that reflected the items usefulness. The "AA" is a broad classification of the item's abilities. The ".2" is a more specific grouping within the "AA" group and relates to how the abilities are used. The "143" is the actual ID number of the item. Finally, the "(85/10)" is a shorthand for comparing the Potential Benefit of using the object vs the Threat or Danger of of using the object.

With Prometheus Labs, I wanted to imply their desire to replicate the object's abilities. Naming the project "Orpheus" is a pretty straightforward reference to what they wanted to do.

The final one is UIU. With this, a complex, unintelligible serial number seems perfect for a government agency. UI is the "casefile" or cereal number for the incident, whereas "OBJ" signifies that the case is related to an item (rather than event). With this inclusion, I wanted to imply that this item and it's abilities were not as secret as the Foundation might like.

But, despite everything that I've said, I kept it vague for a reason. My goal here was to spark the reader's imagination, so I don't want my intent to be the "cannon" interpretation. If you think it would be more interesting to think of these Aliases in terms of other groups, like ORIA or MC&D, by all means, feel free to!
